div.p: Olmo-3.1-32B / 8xH200 / 64 rollouts per step. MATH runs 48 s/step on a 7B with response_length: 2000 — the gap is model size x tokens generated.
train.py:150 records only step_seconds. Splitting the residual needs phase timers around each call above (~10 lines).

tr.td: drop in-run eval (use the offline pass)

div.p: Concurrency is NOT a lever: 8 vs 64 verifier workers measured 30.1 s vs 30.2 s, because wallclock is the slowest single program, not throughput.
vLLM puts "stop"/"length" in finish_reason; stop_reason is the matched stop STRING and is None for both natural EOS and truncation. So or "stop" labels everything "stop".

All 640 completions report stop while 24% sit exactly at the 8192 cap — those are truncated, usually mid-program, and are trained on as if they finished. It also hides truncation from fidelity_ok() (backend/base.py:70).
train.py:101 LoRA weights -> vLLM not separately measured
train.py:110 CPU only — negligible
train.py:122 -> rl/kl.py:54 backend.ref_logprobs(datums)
a FULL extra forward pass over every datum on the frozen base, every step, to serve kl_coef: 0.02
UNMEASURED — no phase timer
train.py:133-135 micro_batch 64, n_datums ~48 -> 1 call per epoch
train.py:136 -> train.py:87 greedy rollout on the TEST split + the same verifier
measured 4.7 s per eval sample at eval_n: 256 that is ~20 min per eval at eval_every: 5 over 100 steps -> 6.7 h = 58% of the run
accuracy is supposed to come from the OFFLINE CodeContests-O pass over the dumped rollouts (tasks/codecontests.py module docstring)
train.py:148 if save_every train.py:155 save("final") — always, 3.1 GB
envs/base.py:149 policy.predict 64 samples, TP=8
median 2663 tok, p90 8192 24% hit the 8192 cap 72% of text is prose before the code block
envs/base.py:162 pool -> tasks/codecontests.py:143 run_stdin_tests
607/640 finish, median 0.415 s 20/640 (3.2%) hit the 30 s timeout
wallclock ~30 s/step (18%) = the single slowest program
train.py:103 -> run_rlvr.py writes rollouts/step-N.jsonl negligible
